Foxhole will give you hundreds, if not thousands, of hours of gameplay if you enjoy large-scale war games. In terms of hours played per dollar spent, it's one of the best value games I've owned. Overall 9/10

The game isn't perfect. Balancing an asymmetric war game is incredibly difficult, and the developers have made mistakes over the years. However, they have consistently continued to update the game and work on addressing issues raised by the community.

One challenge the developers face is that many players become very attached to their chosen faction. As a result, discussions about balance can sometimes be influenced by faction loyalty, making it difficult to separate genuine balance concerns from faction bias.

When reading negative reviews, it's worth keeping in mind that many come from veteran players with hundreds or even thousands of hours in the game. Some of their criticisms are valid and come from a place of passion for the game, while others are frustrations with specific balance decisions or development choices and others just because they been told to downvote the game by their own regiment leaders because they didn't get what they want.(meh people)

Overall, if you're looking for a unique persistent-war MMO where every bullet, tank, ship, and aircraft is built and supplied by players, Foxhole is absolutely worth trying.

For someone who doesn't have the time to play the game often, and a solo player, merging your only two servers into one massive server was a very poor choice. The one and only experience i had with Able server lasted 5 minutes. I'm still learning the map, so i found what looked like a decent area with groups that might need assistance. I spawn in the bunker, no combat, and i didn't see any other players. Didn't think much of it, figured I'd head out and find supplies from a bunker closer to the action. NO. There were land mines CIRCLING the bunker. Every exit and window. They were ally mines. Why were there mines around a main spawn area? I don't know. Could I have defused them? I don't know. I'm still new to this. Moral of the story. Able server felt like it was owned by heavy RPers and veterans of the game that don't want new players ruining THEIR experience. With Charlie server, at least i felt welcomed as a new player. How do you expect brand new players to get into this if that's what's waiting for them?

I'll flesh this review out eventually but in my time with this game, the designers have consistently made it less fun. Weird niche complaints will get patched urgently while major issues flagged by hundreds of players go unaddressed. This combined with a reticence to communicate (we only get info from them 4 times a year. if we are lucky they remind us after a pop crash that they exist) and the community has grown increasingly factionalized - which turns the selective-listening feedback loop into a death spiral.

The premise is clearly excellent and many of us are addicted as a result, but on account of repeated design and implementation missteps I cannot bring myself to recommend this game. to friends or to strangers.
